Resonator guitars have also been made in Brazil, Australia and Asia.

The resonator guitar is a fretted chordophone modified to be louder: the bridge passes the vibration of the strings to one or more spun metal cones instead of relying on the guitar's soundboard. It was first used to compete with brass and percussion in dance orchestras; later its timbre came to be valued for itself, and it has been used ever since in bluegrass and the blues. There are square-neck and round-neck versions: the square neck is mostly played like a lap steel guitar, the round neck like a traditional or a steel guitar. Bluegrass tradition mostly uses the square neck, the blues the round neck, often with a bottleneck slide.
共鳴吉他琴身可為木製、金屬製，偶爾其他材料；三錐型多為金屬琴身，另有少量木製型號: The body of a resonator guitar may be wood, metal or occasionally another material; three-cone models mostly have metal bodies, with a few wooden ones. The sounding body is a metal cone: the three-cone type uses three aluminium cones with a T-shaped aluminium bar supporting the bridge; the single inverted cone type uses one inverted cone with a round perforated metal coverplate and an eight-legged aluminium spider carrying the bridge; the single-cone biscuit type uses one upright aluminium cone with a wooden biscuit on top carrying the bridge. Some later bodies used wood and fibreglass. The source does not state the materials of the fingerboard, the strings and so on.
共鳴器吉他以弦振動經琴橋傳至旋製金屬錐形共鳴器發聲。方頸款多採膝上鋼棒吉他式演奏: A resonator guitar sounds by passing the vibration of the strings through the bridge into spun metal cones. Square-neck models are mostly played lap-steel style, which needs a high action and a suitable open tuning; round-neck models can be played lap style or like an ordinary guitar, and the action can be set high for a slide or low for fretting. A beginner first chooses the neck type for the way of playing, tunes the instrument and adjusts the action, then sets the strings vibrating with a slide or by fretting them so that the sound reaches the resonator.
共鳴管吉他主要出現在藍草音樂與藍調音樂中，也曾在早期舞蹈管弦樂裡與銅管、打擊樂器: The resonator guitar appears mainly in bluegrass and the blues, and in early dance orchestras it played alongside brass and percussion to raise the volume. In performance the square-neck type is mostly played lap-steel style with a slide stopping the strings, and it is common in bluegrass line-ups; the round-neck type can be played as an ordinary guitar or as a steel guitar, and blues players often use a bottleneck slide. It is used in many parts of the world, and in these genres it has developed a recognisable way of playing.
共鳴管通過精心設計的管道結構，能夠有效擴大打擊樂器的音量並延長音符的餘韻。其音色: Through a carefully designed tube structure, the resonator tube effectively enlarges the volume of a percussion instrument and lengthens the ring of each note. Its timbre is warm and penetrating; the treble is bright and clear, the bass deep and full. The design of the resonator tube gives a balanced sound in every register and avoids an uneven spread of volume. Compared with the piano, it is more penetrating; compared with the direct strike of a xylophone, the resonator tube makes each note rounder and fuller. Through the resonance of the tube a percussion instrument can produce a sound that is both forceful and musical, and the expressive range of the music is greatly increased.
